turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis of the training data

**Where the maxima live.** The target rises monotonically through the dataset's recipe families:
- Low-temperature-only recipes (NT=885, everything else minimal): 225–275 MPa — poor.
- Quench-and-temper recipes (NT≈825–900, THT≈845–865, TT≈550–680): 325–643 MPa — moderate; higher tempering temperature (TT 550→580) and Ni–Cr–Mo alloying help.
- High-Si / high-C variants (Si≈1.5–2.05, C≈0.53–0.63): 688–906 MPa — good but these sit at composition extremes (Si=2.05, C=0.63 are range edges → not robust).
- **Carburizing recipes (NT=930, CT=930, Ct>0, DT≈850–896, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5): 838–1190 MPa — clearly the best family**, occupying the entire top ~30 rows.

**Within the winning family, what drives the top (≥1080 MPa) rows:**
- C low (~0.17–0.23), Si ~0.2–0.35, Mn ~0.5–0.85
- Cr high (~1.1–1.17) or Ni high (~1.6–1.7) — both routes work; Cr≈1.1–1.17 with Mo≈0.15–0.18 appears most often
- Mo 0.15–0.21, Cu modest (~0.07–0.12)
- P, S low-to-mid (≤0.02)
- RedRatio mid-range (~440–860; 690 recurs)
- Inclusion ratings low (dA ≤0.08, dB ≈0–0.01, dC ≈0–0.01)
- Process: Ct anywhere 90–540 (broad), DT≈850–896, Dt 15–70 (broad), QmT 60 or 140 both fine, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5 — all repeated across many top rows, indicating a **broad plateau**, not a sharp peak.

**Robustness choices.** I avoid range edges (Si=2.05, C=0.63, Ni=2.78) and instead take the central, repeatedly-observed values of the top carburizing cluster: C≈0.21, Si≈0.30, Mn≈0.80, Cr≈1.14, Mo≈0.17, RedRatio≈690, mid Ct/DT/Dt, QmT=100 (between the two winning levels 60/140), TT=180 (between 160/200). Every chosen value is surrounded by other high-performing rows, so a ±5% perturbation of any single variable stays inside the plateau.

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=450, DT=890, Dt=50, QmT=100, TT=180, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.3, Mn=0.8, P=0.013, S=0.016, Ni=0.5, Cr=1.14, Cu=0.1, Mo=0.17, RedRatio=690, dA=0.06, dB=0.005, dC=0.005
